newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Ifo index rises as weak mark helps exports.
newsitem.headline: German Ifo index rises as weak mark helps exports.

text.p: Germany's business climate improved for the third month in succession in June, the Ifo economic research institute said on Friday, as the weak mark boosted profits and sentiment in the export sector.
In western Germany, Ifo's business climate index rose to 96.0 from a revised 95.4 in May, outpacing average analysts' forecasts which were for a reading of around 95.7.
According to the index, which draws on the Ifo institute's monthly survey of businesses, conditions also improved in western Germany in June, with the reading up to 88.9 from a revised 87.3 in May.

Analysts said the weakness of the mark, which has declined sharply against the dollar this year, was reflected in the business climate, with export companies seeing higher profits as German goods become cheaper abroad.
"It (the index) is a bit stronger," said Gernot Nerb, economist as Salomon Brothers in Frankfurt.
"The improvement of the business situation reflects a better profit situation. The weak mark and higher export profits are reflected."

The German currency, which touched its lowest point for almost six years earlier this week at around 1.8040 to the dollar, was in slightly better shape after the Ifo numbers but lost out again after Chancellor Helmut Kohl said the recent strength of the dollar was not an "earth-shaking matter". By 1041 GMT the mark was at 1.7995 to the dollar.

Analysts at UBS in Frankfurt said any continuance of mark weakness was likely to offer more good news for export firms in the coming months, and could slowly begin to filter through to Germany's floundering labour market.

"If ... the mark remains weak, leading to further improvements in export prospects, then this constellation might eventually lead to a significant upward revision in production plans and a turn in the labour market in the quarters ahead," they said in a commentary on the Ifo numbers.
In eastern Germany, however, Ifo's June business climate reading eased back slightly with the index at 103.6 from an upward revised 103.7 in May.

"The east German figure shows construction in the east is still not so good. In spite of the dollar rise, the expectations in west Germany are not so good," said Matthias Haffner, economist at BZW in Frankfurt.
